findings.title: Constructor validates grantType twice, never validates rawTokenId
findings.body: In AccessTokenContext constructor both null-checks use grantType, the second message says rawTokenId but still checks grantType. A null rawTokenId therefore passes validation and later encodeTokenId produces a jti ending in ':null' and getRawTokenId returns null, corrupting token identity and breaking round-trip decode.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut breaks existing grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory adds abstract String getShortcut() with no default implementation. Any existing third-party or downstream OAuth2GrantTypeFactory that implements the old interface will fail to compile and at runtime will throw AbstractMethodError, preventing server startup. A default method returning unknown sentinel or requiring migration would preserve compatibility.

findings.title: grantType cached at construction becomes stale and can NPE
findings.body: Context constructor caches grantType via formParams.getFirst(grant_type) but setFormParams can later replace formParams without updating the cached field, so getGrantType returns stale value while getFormParams returns new value and tokens are encoded with wrong grant. Previously the constructor only assigned formParams so null was tolerated; now a null formParams causes NullPointerException in the constructor.

findings.title: Removed public copy constructor Context(Context)
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted. Custom OAuth2GrantType implementations or extensions that copied context via new Context(context) will no longer compile and break source and binary compatibility with no deprecation or replacement.

findings.title: Decoder throws on malformed token IDs instead of graceful fallback
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId returns UNKNOWN context for IDs without colon but throws IllegalArgumentException for IDs with colon and wrong prefix length or unknown shortcuts. When this decoder is used on jti values taken from presented JWTs for introspection/userInfo/session optimization, attacker-supplied or foreign IDs will cause unhandled exceptions and 500s instead of falling back to UNKNOWN and doing normal lookup.

findings.title: No validation that grant shortcuts are 2 chars and colon-free
findings.body: postInit copies arbitrary strings from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut into maps with no check for length 2 or absence of colon, while the decoder assumes exactly 6-char prefix split as 2+2+2 and uses colon as delimiter. A custom grant with 3-char shortcut or colon produces token IDs that can never be decoded and validation comparing map sizes does not catch length violations.

findings.title: Lazy grant map refresh races and can clobber mappings
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut do non-atomic check-then-put on shared ConcurrentHashMaps and blindly overwrite shortcut to grant mappings without collision detection. Concurrent token issuance and decoding can interleave, lose updates, or overwrite one grant's shortcut with another's, permanently corrupting decode for the victim grant.

findings.title: Access token ID matcher has inverted logic and wrong offsets
findings.body: isAccessTokenId splits on colon then checks items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut) and returns false when equal. Correct grant position for 6-char prefix on+tt+gt is substring 4,6, and logic should fail when not equal. As written any UUID-suffixed ID passes regardless of grant and short prefixes can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so tests never verify grant encoding.
